relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with a diagnosis of SSADH deficiency: "At 12 years of age, Ms. A was diagnosed with SSADH deficiency"; she was diagnosed biochemically and "Genotyping was not performed."
method_note: Read the paper directly; JSON assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans, and every span checked verbatim by script. No tables in the paper. Scope: Ms. A (diagnosis of SSADH deficiency, confirmed by urinary organic acids; genotyping not performed, so no variant rows); her younger brother (diagnosed with 'the same condition', so an affected relative; no other detail); and the single individual from Knerr et al. [9] mentioned in the Discussion with features (anxiety, OCD symptoms) and treatment, included under the v4 passing-mention rule (the paper does not state this individual's diagnosis in the same sentence; context is SSADH deficiency patients, so disease_label left not reported). Aggregate figures from Knerr et al. [9] (11 of 33) and Lapalme-Remis et al. [10] (12 of 25) are group counts and get no rows. The mother is mentioned (consent; Ms. A's fears of harm to her) but is not described as tested or affected, so no row. n_patients_reported left null because no patient with an ALDH5A1 variant is described (genotyping not performed). Ms. A's last-evaluation age is the 26 years in 'Ms. A is a 26-year-old'; vital status left not reported (not stated explicitly). Age 4 is the diagnosis of epilepsy and global developmental delay, not of SSADH deficiency (age 12). Extrapyramidal side effects, social withdrawal and hypersomnolence are recorded as observed features with a note that the paper attributes them to the adjunct medications. Checklist: 'speech or language impairment' and 'dystonia' marked observed from 'Her speech was slow, had low tone and was mildly dystonic.'; hypotonia left not reported (mildly elevated tone at 22 does not state hypotonia absent); gross or fine motor deficits left not reported (gait findings and tremor were not mapped to that item); agitation not mapped to aggression; hypersomnolence (drug side effect) not mapped to sleep disturbances. No contradictions found.
